newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks leap higher in early trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks leap higher in early trade.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks leaped to life early Thursday morning on bullish sentiment inspired by Wall Street's record run and faith in the long-term earnings potential of local property developers, brokers said.
"The market is taking its lead from the U.S.," said Julian Ings-Chambers, assistant director at BZW Securities Asia. "And there is nothing negative on the horizon."
The Hang Seng Index put on 87 points to 13,550 in early morning trade. The index shot ahead 120 points to a early high of 13,583.48 before falling back. Turnover climbed to HK$1.55 billion.
"The rally this morning is broad-based in the blue chip sector," said Ings Chambers,

The local market took its lead from the Dow's 103.52-point surge to 6,961.63 on Wednesday. But analysts said factors boosting Wall Street, such as positive outlooks for technology stocks and mutual funds inflows, had little long-term impact on Hong Kong.
"The tech stock rally is not related to Hong Kong," said Steven Chu, technical analyst at Sassoon Securities. "So we may see further divergence between Hong Kong and New York."
On a technical basis the Hang Seng was unlikely to rechallenge its all time high of 14,004.93, Chu added.
"The Hang Seng has made a short-term bottom, so we should have a good rebound today, but turnover remains weak, so the rebound may be limited," he said.
Brokers said there was some caution due to the continued rise in the U.S. long bond yield and in advance of the latest set of U.S. inflation figures due out on Friday.
The property sector far outperformed all other blue chips sectors. Red chips were mixed and H shares were generally positive.
Sun Hung Kai Properties jumped HK$2.00 to HK$91.25 and Henderson Land strengthened HK$0.75 to HK$71.75.
Brokers said investors continued to seek banking giant HSBC Holdings as a way to get greater, inexpensive exposure to the local property development earnings. The share rose HK$1.00 to HK$188.50.
CITIC Pacific added HK$0.10 to HK$38.50 and Shanghai Industrial jumped HK$0.55 to HK$29.45. H share Guangdong Kelon put on HK$0.15 to HK$6.35.
The February Hang Seng Index futures contract was trading 135 points higher at 13,555 after 30 minutes of trade, a slight premium to the cash market.
